Project rules (always apply):
- Never run a destructive git command (reset --hard, clean -f, push --force, branch -D, checkout .). Prefer reversible operations; if a destructive one is truly needed, stop and confirm first.
- Before your first write, create a branch for the task and do the work there. Never commit to the default branch. Branch names follow type/kebab-description, where type is one of feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, release, docs.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): subject, where type is one of feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, ci, build, perf, style.
- Never credit an AI assistant in published text: no Co-Authored-By for an assistant, no generated-with signature, no robot emoji. The work is published under the human author's name alone.
- Everything written into a file is in English, always, whatever language the request was written in. This covers documentation, comments, docstrings, identifiers and commit messages. Only the reply in conversation follows the language of the request.
- Markdown is soft-wrapped: one paragraph, one line. Never hard-wrap prose at a column limit, and do not copy the wrapping of the file you are editing. Rewrapping belongs to whatever renders the text, which is the only thing that knows the reader's width.
- Append to the operations log with bin/oplog, never by editing ops/log.md directly. The script writes the entry in the required shape and keeps the file append-only; a hand edit silently breaks both.
- Before answering a question about this project's conventions, open CONVENTIONS.md and answer from it. Do not answer from general knowledge; this project's conventions are deliberately not the common ones.

This project has no CONTRIBUTING.md. Write one explaining how to set the project up, how to run the tests, and what to do before opening a pull request.

+# Contributing
+
+## Project Setup
+
+### Requirements
+- Python 3.7+
+
+### Installation
+
+1. Clone the repository:
+```bash
+git clone <repository-url>
+cd <repo-name>
+```
+
+2. Create and activate a virtual environment:
+```bash
+python -m venv venv
+source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
+```
+
+3. Install dependencies (as needed for development):
+```bash
+pip install -e .  # If setup.py exists
+# or
+pip install -r requirements.txt  # If requirements.txt exists
+```
+
+## Running Tests
+
+Tests should be added to the `tests/` directory. When tests exist, run them with:
+```bash
+pytest
+```
+
+or
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest
+```
+
+## Before Opening a Pull Request
+
+### Branch Setup
+Create a feature branch from `main`:
+```bash
+git checkout main
+git pull
+git checkout -b <type>/<kebab-description>
+```
+
+Branch types: `feature`, `bugfix`, `hotfix`, `chore`, `release`, `docs`
+
+Example: `feature/inventory-reconciliation`
+
+### Code Quality
+- Follow Python naming conventions (PEP 8)
+- Write clear, concise functions with docstrings where needed
+- Add or update tests for your changes
+- Ensure no syntax errors by running your code
+
+### Commits
+Follow Conventional Commits for your commit messages:
+```
+<type>(<scope>): <subject>
+
+<optional body>
+```
+
+Types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `ci`, `build`, `perf`, `style`
+
+Examples:
+- `feat(inventory): add reconciliation logic`
+- `fix(pricing): handle missing snapshot data`
+- `test: add tests for shipment planner`
+
+### PR Checklist
+- [ ] Code changes are on a feature branch (not `master` or `main`)
+- [ ] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits
+- [ ] Tests added or updated for new functionality
+- [ ] No Python syntax errors
+- [ ] README updated if behavior changed
+- [ ] Branch is up to date with `main`
+
+### Before Pushing
+```bash
+git push -u origin <type>/<kebab-description>
+```
+
+Create a pull request on GitHub with a clear description of your changes.
